subject: Biology
central_question: How does division of labour among cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems create the coordinated structure and function of a vertebrate such as the frog?
in_scope_units: Organisation from cells to tissues, organs, and organ systems and the resulting division of labour.
Frog habitat, poikilothermy, camouflage, aestivation, and hibernation.
External morphology of the frog, including skin, body regions, limbs, sense structures, and sexual dimorphism.
Digestive system and digestion in the frog.
Respiratory system and cutaneous, buccal, and pulmonary respiration.
Closed blood vascular and lymphatic systems, heart, circulation, blood, and portal systems.
Excretory system, kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, cloaca, and ureotelism.
Neural and endocrine coordination and sense organs.
Male and female reproductive systems, external fertilisation, tadpole development, and ecological importance.
banned_topics: Detailed histology of the four animal tissue types
Comparative anatomy of other vertebrate classes
Molecular mechanisms of hormones and nerve impulses

known_pitfalls.claim: A tissue is simply a group of identical cells.
known_pitfalls.correction: A tissue is a group of similar cells together with intercellular substances performing one or more functions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Frogs maintain a constant internal body temperature.
known_pitfalls.correction: Frogs are poikilotherms, so body temperature varies with environmental temperature.

known_pitfalls.claim: A frog drinks water through its mouth.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter states that a frog absorbs water through its moist skin.

known_pitfalls.claim: Frogs respire only through lungs on land and gills in water.
known_pitfalls.correction: Adult frogs use skin in water and skin, buccal cavity, and lungs on land; skin is especially important during dormancy.

known_pitfalls.claim: The frog heart has four chambers.
known_pitfalls.correction: It has two atria and one ventricle.

known_pitfalls.claim: Male and female frog ureters have exactly the same reproductive role.
known_pitfalls.correction: Male ureters function as urinogenital ducts, while female ureters carry urine and the oviducts open separately into the cloaca.

recommended_example_progression: Figure 7.1: identify external features and sexual dimorphism in a frog.
NCERT Exercise 1 and Figure 7.2: trace and label the digestive system.
Section 7.2.2: compare cutaneous, buccal, and pulmonary respiration.
NCERT Exercise 2: explain the function of ureters in male and female frogs.
Figures 7.3 and 7.4: compare male and female reproductive systems and trace external fertilisation and metamorphosis.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the end-of-chapter EXERCISES 1–2, supported by Figures 7.1–7.4 for morphology and organ-system interpretation.
